anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, references D9 and D10 are populated with optocoupler / digital-isolator symbols (KiCad 'Isolator' graphics with 'Input 1/Input 2' LED pins and 'Output/Output 3' phototransistor pins), and their input pins are wired straight across the CAN differential pairs (D10 across CAN0_P/CAN0_N next to transceiver U11; D9 across CAN1_P/CAN1_N next to transceiver U10). No CDSOT23-SM712 TVS-array part appears anywhere in the drawing; the only TVS arrays present (U4/U23, TPD4E1U06DCKR, drawn with CH1..CH4/VN/VP pins) are on the Ethernet lines, not the CAN lines.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states these references are transient/ESD protection: 'D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N ... the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.' A 4-pin back-to-back TVS clamp (not an optocoupler) should sit across each CAN pair.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N ... the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.

CAN BUS sheet: D10 (and D9 on the CAN1 half) drawn as an optocoupler/Isolator symbol with 'Input 2'/'Input 1' tied to CAN0_P/CAN0_N (CAN1_P/CAN1_N) and 'Output'/'Output 3' to GND; no SM712/CDSOT23 part present on the CAN nets.

anomalies.impact: Two-fold: (1) the CAN buses lose their specified ESD/transient clamp, exposing U10/U11 and the field cabling to damage; (2) an optocoupler LED placed across a CAN differential pair conducts during the dominant state (≈2 V differential vs ≈1.2 V LED Vf), loading/clamping the bus so the transceivers cannot drive a valid dominant bit, i.e. CAN0 and CAN1 communication would fail.

parsed.summary: The CAN-bus protection parts D9/D10 are drawn as optocouplers wired across the CAN differential pairs instead of the specified CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays, removing the documented ESD/transient protection and, worse, loading the CAN lines so the buses cannot communicate; this is the one deviation the drawing supports against the spec.
